relevance_note: A clinical review (CME 'Approach to the patient') opening with one first-hand case, 'He was diagnosed with Tangier disease', a 22-yr-old South Asian man; no ABCA1 variant is reported for him.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; JSON built with a short script in the scratch directory from values I transcribed; every span checked verbatim by script. In scope: the single case-vignette patient (diagnosis of Tangier disease, clinical/biochemical; no genetic testing or ABCA1 variant reported, so no variant rows) and his mother and father, described with HDL-C levels ('mildly reduced HDL-C', 26 and 22 mg/dl). Left out: the 'two siblings first identified' on Tangier island (ref 24; only the defining low HDL-C and the diagnosis, no individual-level fact beyond it), the Tangier patient whose tonsils are pictured in Fig. 2C (ref 26; image only), and the apoA-I-deficiency cases (other gene). Lipid values reported without interpretation (LDL-C 49 mg/dl, triglycerides 184 mg/dl, total cholesterol 92 mg/dl) were not turned into low LDL or hypertriglyceridemia; those checklist items are not reported. 'normal sensation and reflexes' was recorded under D-27 as abnormal sensation and abnormal reflexes excluded, and used to exclude the checklist items reduced tendon reflexes and reduced deep sensation; peripheral neuropathy itself was left not reported (the plan is 'surveillance of peripheral neuropathy'). 'no xanthomas' was not used to exclude the broader checklist item skin lipid deposits; 'no plaque' on carotid ultrasound was not used to exclude non-coronary atherosclerotic arterial disease. 'He had no family history of cardiovascular disease' was applied as a group statement to both parents (cardiovascular disease excluded; checklist coronary artery disease excluded, inferred from group statement); non-coronary arterial disease left not reported. Age 22 is the age at referral/evaluation; the paper gives no explicit age at diagnosis, so age_at_diagnosis is not reported. Vital status not stated. No contradictions found.
